bibliography.checked_against: the article's first page and Crossref
bibliography.note: Barthel, Cooke, Svec, Suski, Bunt, Phelan & Philipp 2008, Journal of Fish Biology 73: 829–852 (issue 4 per Crossref), doi:10.1111/j.1095-8649.2008.01972.x — as in the reference.

claims.claim: Millers Lake, Ontario, is a 45-ha lake (on a river)
claims.quote: Millers Lake, a 45 ha widening of the Mississippi River, Ontario
claims.conditions: the Mississippi River of eastern Ontario; study reach also includes a 1.5-km pool-and-riffle section directly upstream

claims.claim: some bass lived in the lake all year while others ran up the river in spring to spawn and returned before winter
claims.location: p. 835 (PDF p. 7), Telemetry study, and Table I (PDF p. 8); p. 838 (PDF p. 10)
claims.quote: a migratory pattern with potamodromous movements from the lake into the river in the spring
claims.conditions: 3-year radio telemetry from May 2000, 29 adults: females 3 lake-resident and 10 potamodromous, males 8 and 8; each fish kept to one pattern; by late November all but one male were back in the lake

claims.claim: most males stayed faithful to river or lake for life
claims.location: p. 838 (PDF p. 10), Nest-site fidelity; abstract p. 829
claims.quote: The vast majority of the 128 males that spawned in multiple years (123 males, 96%)
claims.conditions: snorkel nest surveys 1997–2004; of 543 males that completed their reproductive lives in the system, most spawned in only one season; of the 128 that spawned in more than one year, 123 (96 %) used the same habitat every year (51 lake, 72 river), 5 used both
claims.note: Precisely: 96 % of males that spawned in more than one year; most males spawned only once.

claims.claim: about half nested within 20 m of their previous nest
claims.location: p. 838 (PDF p. 10), Nest-site fidelity, and Fig. 2
claims.quote: nearly half of the nesting decisions in the river, and just more than half
claims.conditions: 110 nesting decisions of 82 males nesting in successive years only in the river and 112 of 67 males only in the lake, 1997–2004; distance to the previous year's nest
claims.note: Unit is nesting decisions of males that nested in successive years, not all males. River males nested closer: 85 % within 100 m vs 65 % in the lake.

notes: The paper marks this '(Barthel et al. 2008, abstract)': the full text is now read and confirms each part, so the 'abstract' tag can go. Other values: potamodromous males entered the river 8–13 days before the first spawn (median 11); 24 of 29 tracked fish wintered in a small area in the deepest part of the lake (Bunt et al. 2003); most frequent age at maturation for river males 4 years. A small internal inconsistency in the source (not the paper's): 128 multi-year spawners (123 single-habitat) vs 82 + 67 = 149 males in the nest-site analysis.
